lines.trans: Nagiyev got awfully generous today, don't you find?
The main thing for him is to show off in front of Elya and everyone.
In a word, he is just a typical actor.
Listen, but you have known him longer.
Did he ever give such expensive gifts to anyone before?
When he was courting Vika, he gave her a car.
Wait, what are you hinting at to me right now?
That man holds nothing sacred in life.
He even cheated on his own wife at his wedding!
Oh come on, what a dark-minded man you are!
Katya, forgive me for bothering you on your birthday.

examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это будет большой фильм о моей жизни.
examples.trans: It will be a big movie about my life.

examples.text: У этого человека нет ничего святого в жизни.
examples.trans: That man holds nothing sacred in life.

examples.text: Никаких больше страховок в моей жизни!
examples.trans: No more insurance policies in my life!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костик, ну попробуй, даже я кусочек съела!
examples.trans: Kostik, just try it, even I ate a piece!

examples.text: Он даже на свадьбе изменил собственной жене!
examples.trans: He even cheated on his own wife at his wedding!

examples.text: Даже ребёнок знает.
examples.trans: Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вадьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wedding' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он даже на свадьбе изменил собственной жене!
examples.trans: He even cheated on his own wife at his wedding!

examples.text: Посмотри фильм Свадьба по скайпу.
examples.trans: Watch the movie Wedding on Skype.

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?

meanings.en: to cheat on, to be unfaithful to
meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'changed', paired with 'изменять'.

examples.text: Он даже на свадьбе изменил собственной жене!
examples.trans: He even cheated on his own wife at his wedding!

examples.text: Эдик, я хотела тебе изменить.
examples.trans: Edik, I wanted to cheat on you.

examples.text: Это ничего не изменит.
examples.trans: That won't change anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own, proper').

examples.text: Он даже на свадьбе изменил собственной жене!
examples.trans: He even cheated on his own wife at his wedding!

examples.text: Твои собственные глаза.
examples.trans: Your own eyes.

examples.text: Твои собственные глаза!
examples.trans: Your own eyes!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты мне нужен на час или два.
examples.trans: I need you for an hour or two.

examples.text: Здесь моя законная жена рядом ходит!
examples.trans: My lawful wife walks around right near here!

examples.text: Но только если жена нас не увидит!
examples.trans: But only if my wife does not see us!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я четыре года назад порезал себе палец.
examples.trans: Four years ago I cut my finger.

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

examples.text: Да ты лучше себе сразу голову сломай!
examples.trans: You might as well break your own head right away!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

examples.text: Хотите скинуться на подарок вместе с нами?
examples.trans: Would you like to chip in for the gift with us?

examples.text: Ты мне нужен на час или два.
examples.trans: I need you for an hour or two.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.text: Мы скидываемся по тысяче рублей, как обычно.
examples.trans: We are chipping in a thousand rubles each, as usual.

examples.text: Я же вчера сказал, больше никаких встреч.
examples.trans: I told you yesterday, no more meetings.

examples.text: Сеня, как думаешь, что Кате подарить?
examples.trans: Senya, what do you think I should give Katya?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dark').

examples.text: Да ну тебя, какой же ты тёмный человек!
examples.trans: Oh come on, what a dark-minded man you are!

examples.text: На нём были большие тёмные очки.
examples.trans: He was wearing large dark glasses.

examples.text: Он просто наденет тёмные чёрные очки.
examples.trans: He will simply put on dark black glasses.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Катя, прости, что беспокою в день рождения.
examples.trans: Katya, forgive me for bothering you on your birthday.

examples.text: Простите, вы кто?
examples.trans: Excuse me, who are you?

examples.text: Прости меня.
examples.trans: Forgive me.

беспокоить.gloss: to bother, to disturb; to worry

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bother, to disturb; to worry', paired with 'побеспокоить'.

examples.text: Не хочу вас беспокоить.
examples.trans: I don't want to bother you.

examples.text: Меня это беспокоит.
examples.trans: That worries me.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А на следующий день он страховку оформил.
examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

examples.text: А сегодня последний день этой моей страховки.
examples.trans: And today is the very last day of this insurance of mine.

examples.text: Если палец будет сломан, я получу деньги.
examples.trans: If my finger is broken, I will get money.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'birthday, birth' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вообще-то сегодня день рождения у твоей дочери.
examples.trans: Actually today is your daughter's birthday.

examples.text: Доченька, дорогая моя, с днём рождения!
examples.trans: My darling daughter, happy birthday!

examples.text: Дорогие друзья, сегодня у Кати день рождения!
examples.trans: Dear friends, today is Katya's birthday!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: По-моему, это просто отличный и выгодный бизнес.
examples.trans: In my opinion, it is simply great and profitable business.

examples.text: Лёва, ты самый щедрый из нас человек.
examples.trans: Lyova, you are the most generous person among us.

examples.text: А мне, стало быть, близкий родственник.
examples.trans: And to me, therefore, a close relative.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проведём время в тесном семейном кругу.
examples.trans: We will spend time in a close family circle.

examples.text: Ваш гостиничный номер уже полностью готов.
examples.trans: Your hotel room is already completely ready.

examples.text: Хорошо, проводите меня до моего номера.
examples.trans: Alright, escort me to my room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are asking for', paired with 'спросить'.

examples.text: Из номера спрашивают, сколько ещё ждать заказ.
examples.trans: They are asking from the room how much longer to wait for the order.

examples.text: Я вас спрашиваю!
examples.trans: I'm asking you!

examples.text: Он всегда спрашивает.
examples.trans: He always asks.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Из номера спрашивают, сколько ещё ждать заказ.
examples.trans: They are asking from the room how much longer to wait for the order.

examples.text: Ого, сколько лет, сколько зим, привет!
examples.trans: Whoa, long time no see, hello!

examples.text: Сколько жвачки!
examples.trans: So much gum!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из номера спрашивают, сколько ещё ждать заказ.
examples.trans: They are asking from the room how much longer to wait for the order.

examples.text: Подожди, ведь это ещё далеко не всё.
examples.trans: Wait, after all that is far from everything.

examples.text: Какая ещё Катя, о ком ты говоришь?
examples.trans: What Katya, who are you talking about?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.text: А мой подарок не заставит себя ждать.
examples.trans: And my gift will not keep you waiting.

examples.text: Из номера спрашивают, сколько ещё ждать заказ.
examples.trans: They are asking from the room how much longer to wait for the order.

examples.text: Не жди меня.
examples.trans: Don't wait for me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здесь моя законная жена рядом ходит!
examples.trans: My lawful wife walks around right near here!

examples.text: Из номера спрашивают, сколько ещё ждать заказ.
examples.trans: They are asking from the room how much longer to wait for the order.

examples.text: Ну что, доченька, ты уже отдала заказ?
examples.trans: Well, sweetheart, did you already deliver the order?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вообще-то сегодня день рождения у твоей дочери.
examples.trans: Actually today is your daughter's birthday.

examples.text: Я же вчера сказал, больше никаких встреч.
examples.trans: I told you yesterday, no more meetings.

examples.text: А праздновать мы будем сегодня вечером.
examples.trans: And we will celebrate tonight.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Положи туда два сахара и свежие сливки.
examples.trans: Put two sugars and fresh cream in it.

examples.text: Ты мне нужен на час или два.
examples.trans: I need you for an hour or two.

examples.text: Ладно, давай двадцать тысяч, и по рукам.
examples.trans: Fine, make it twenty thousand, and we have a deal.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minutes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Через две минуты всё отнесу!
examples.trans: I will bring everything up in two minutes!

examples.text: Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Одну минуту!
examples.trans: Just a minute!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дима, твои шутки становятся всё слабее.
examples.trans: Dima, your jokes are getting weaker and weaker.

examples.text: Ведь он тебе всё-таки родной отец.
examples.trans: After all, he is still your own father.

examples.text: Я ради семьи на всё сегодня готова.
examples.trans: For the sake of the family I am ready for anything today.

meanings.en: to carry, deliver something to a place
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry to, take to', paired with 'относить'.

examples.text: Через две минуты всё отнесу!
examples.trans: I will bring everything up in two minutes!

examples.text: Я сам отнесу блюдо в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry the dish into the dining room myself.

examples.text: Отнеси документы шефу.
examples.trans: Take the documents to the boss.
